sections.Kurzabstract: The CSIP is a self-report questionnaire used to assess interpersonal problems in adults. It is a freely accessible supplement and alternative to the established IIP-C and, like it, is based on the interpersonal circumplex (IPC). It comprises 64 items assigned to the following eight scales: too autocratic/dominant (PA), too quarrelsome/competitive (BC), too dismissive/cold (DE), too introverted/socially avoidant (FG), too insecure/submissive (HI), too exploitable/submissive (JK), too caring/friendly (LM), too expressive/intrusive (NO). Reliability: McDonald's omega values were between ω = .85 and ω = .94. Test-retest correlations were between rtt = .70 and rtt = .87. Validity: Findings on structural and convergent validity as well as criterion validity are available.
sections.Diagnostische Zielsetzung: The CSIP is a self-report questionnaire used to assess interpersonal problems in adults. It is a freely accessible supplement and alternative to the established IIP-C and, like it, is based on the interpersonal circumplex (IPC). According to this model, interpersonal behaviours are arranged on a circle with two axes, control (vertical) and affiliation (horizontal). The blend of the two dimensions yields eight specific interpersonal styles.
sections.Aufbau: The CSIP comprises 64 items that are answered on a four-point scale ("0 = stimme nicht zu", "1 = stimme ein wenig zu", "2 = stimme zu", "3 = stimme voll und ganz zu"). Eight items each are assigned to the following eight scales: too autocratic/dominant (PA), too quarrelsome/competitive (BC), too dismissive/cold (DE), too introverted/socially avoidant (FG), too insecure/submissive (HI), too exploitable/submissive (JK), too caring/friendly (LM), too expressive/intrusive (NO).
sections.Grundlagen und Konstruktion: The German version of the CSIP is based on the English original version by Boudreaux et al. (2018). The translation was carried out by two authors, who first each produced a version independently and then merged them into a joint version. This was back-translated by a native speaker and revised using feedback from Aidan C. Wright, one of the original authors. The final version was confirmed by Aidan C. Wright and examined psychometrically.
sections.Empirische Prüfung und Gütekriterien:
Reliability: McDonald's omega values were between ω = .85 and ω = .94. Test-retest correlations were between rtt = .70 and rtt = .87.
Validity: The CSIP was validated on a population sample that was large with regard to gender and age. Findings on structural and convergent validity as well as criterion validity are available.
Norms: No norm values are available. However, comparison values from a large German sample are available in the form of means and standard deviations.
sections.Testkonzept/Theoretischer Hintergrund:
The Circumplex Scales of Interpersonal Problems - German version (CSIP) are used to assess interpersonal problems in adults. These play a central role in the development and maintenance of various mental disorders and are a decisive feature of personality disorders.
The CSIP was developed as a freely accessible supplement and alternative to the established "Inventory of Interpersonal Problems - Circumplex" (IIP-C). The German translation is based on the English original version by Boudreaux et al. (2018).
The CSIP is based on the interpersonal circumplex (IPC), a circular model with two orthogonal axes that represent the basic dimensions of interpersonal behaviour: control (vertical axis) and affiliation (horizontal axis). Control comprises behaviours ranging from dominance to submissiveness. Affiliation comprises behaviours ranging from closeness to distance. The blends of these dimensions yield eight specific interpersonal styles: too autocratic/dominant (PA), too quarrelsome/competitive (BC), too dismissive/cold (DE), too introverted/socially avoidant (FG), too insecure/submissive (HI), too exploitable/submissive (JK), too caring/friendly (LM), too expressive/intrusive (NO).
sections.Testkonzept/Testaufbau:
The CSIP is a self-report questionnaire consisting of 64 items with a four-point response scale ("0 = stimme nicht zu", "1 = stimme ein wenig zu", "2 = stimme zu", "3 = stimme voll und ganz zu"). It comprises eight scales corresponding to those of the IIP-C, with eight items each:
PA: too autocratic/dominant (items 1, 9, 17, 25, 33, 41, 49, 57)
BC: too quarrelsome/competitive (items 2, 10, 18, 26, 34, 42, 50, 58)
DE: too dismissive/cold (items 3, 11, 19, 27, 35, 43, 51, 59)
FG: too introverted/socially avoidant (items 4, 12, 20, 28, 36, 44, 52, 60)
HI: too insecure/submissive (items 5, 13, 21, 29, 37, 45, 53, 61)
JK: too exploitable/submissive (items 6, 14, 22, 30, 38, 46, 54, 62)
LM: too caring/friendly (items 7, 15, 23, 31, 39, 47, 55, 63)
NO: too expressive/intrusive (items 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56, 64)
sections.Testkonzept/Auswertungsmodus:
To assess interpersonal styles, the means of the eight questionnaire scales can be calculated. The average of all 64 items is interpreted as general interpersonal distress. In addition, scores on the two superordinate dimensions control and affiliation can be calculated using the following formulas:
Control = PA + (NO × .71) + (BC × .71)-(FG × .71) - (JK × .71) - HI
Affiliation = LM + (NO × .71) + (JK × .71) - (BC × .71) - (FG × .71) - DE
sections.Testkonzept/Auswertungshilfen: No scoring aids are needed for manual scoring. A scoring aid as an Excel file as well as scoring scripts for SPSS and R are available.
sections.Testkonzept/Auswertungszeit: Scoring takes 1 minute electronically and 3 minutes by hand.
sections.Durchführung/Testformen: The present version of the CSIP is the German translation of the English-language original questionnaire of the same name by Boudreaux et al. (2018). A short form with 32 items is under development.
sections.Durchführung/Altersbereiche: The CSIP was validated in persons aged 18 to 90 years.
sections.Durchführung/Durchführungszeit: The average administration time is 4 minutes.
sections.Durchführung/Material:
The CSIP can be used in paper-pencil or digital form.
In addition to the present documentation of the procedure, the test package contains the questionnaire with information on which items belong to which subscale. An Excel file as a scoring aid as well as scoring scripts for SPSS and R are also available for download.
sections.Durchführung/Instruktion: The instruction can be found on the questionnaire. It reads: „Im Folgenden finden Sie eine Liste mit persönlichen Problemen, über die Menschen häufig in ihrem Leben berichten. Dazu gehören eigene Gedanken, Gefühle oder Verhaltensweisen, die emotional belastend sein können und häufig Beziehungen beeinträchtigen. Lesen Sie jede Aussage sorgfältig durch und geben Sie an, wie stark Sie das jeweilige Problem erleben. Bitte markieren Sie Ihre Zustimmung auf der angegebenen Skala.“
sections.Durchführung/Durchführungsvoraussetzunge:
The test situation should be as standardized as possible. The questionnaire should be completed alone and in a quiet environment. The participants should have basic reading ability.
Scoring and interpretation should be carried out by professionally qualified and experienced personnel.
sections.Testkonstruktion:
The translation of the original questionnaire into German was carried out by two authors, who first each produced a version independently and then worked out a joint version from them. After back-translation by a native English speaker, the version was revised based on feedback from Aidan C. Wright, one of the authors of the original version, and finally confirmed by him.
The CSIP was validated in two waves one month apart on a large German sample (NT1 = 677, NT2 = 514) (see Table 1 under "Reliability"), which is representative of the German general population with regard to gender and age. Of the participants, 49.8% were female and 50.2% male. Age ranged from 18 to 90 years (M = 52.47).
The psychometric properties of the CSIP were examined with the Circular Stochastic Process Model For The Circumplex (SPMC) according to Browne (1992). This is a structural equation approach with which the circularity of the scales can be tested (i.e. whether they can be mapped in a three-dimensional space in a factor-analytic sense and whether their correlations show a circular arrangement). By means of an extension of the SPMC that allows covariates to be integrated (SPMC-E; Nagy et al., 2019), convergent validity in relation to the IIP-C was examined. In addition, internal consistencies and test-retest correlations (time interval: 1 month) of the scales were calculated.
Information on test construction and validation is described in detail in Wester et al. (2025, submitted).
sections.Gütekriterien/Objektivität: The objectivity of the CSIP is ensured by standardized specifications in administration, scoring and interpretation.

sections.Gütekriterien/Validität:
Validity was examined by Wester and colleagues (2025, submitted). The correlations between the scales followed the expected circular pattern, and the scale positions deviated only slightly from the positions theoretically assumed on the IPC. This structure proved to be stable over time.
The convergent validity of the CSIP was confirmed by comparisons with the established IIP-C. The scales of both instruments correlated highly with one another, and their positions in the IPC largely agreed. However, differences between the two questionnaires emerged with regard to the assessment of interpersonal problems at the dominance pole. In the comparison of the scales' content, it was found that the CSIP scales PA and BC capture more extreme forms of dominant behaviour than the corresponding IIP-C scales. It is therefore assumed that the CSIP is better suited than the IIP-C to distinguish between more strongly maladaptive forms of dominant behaviour.
Significant associations were also found between the German CSIP scales and clinically relevant characteristics such as dysphoria and level of personality functioning.
sections.Gütekriterien/Normierung: So far, only comparison values for the total sample are available (see Table 1; as of: June 2025).
sections.Anwendungsmöglichkeiten: The CSIP enables the assessment of interpersonal problems in adults. The information obtained can be used in individual diagnostics, for example to identify problematic interpersonal tendencies and to assess treatment progress. In research, it enables, for example, the investigation of the association between interpersonal problems and mental disorders. Unlike the IIP-C, the CSIP is a freely accessible instrument for this purpose. In addition, the results of the validation study indicate that the CSIP differentiates extreme behaviours in the dominant range better and could thus be better suited to assessing interpersonal styles.
sections.Bewertung: The German version of the CSIP shows good psychometric quality criteria and is thus a suitable instrument for assessing interpersonal problems. It is freely accessible and can be used as an alternative or supplement to the IIP-C. However, the differences between the CSIP and the IIP-C with regard to the measurement of dominant behaviour should be taken into account. In addition, the validation of the CSIP was carried out on a non-clinical sample. In future, the psychometric properties of the CSIP should also be examined in a clinical sample. The development of a short form of the CSIP is also desirable, as with 64 items it is relatively long.
